tasks.description: Scaffold repository: layout, continuity files, subagents, commands

ingest/dma.py: download Danish AIS for a date range, land as Parquet partitioned by date. Real day landed 2026-09-16: 2024-06-05, 17,239,519 rows, 4,878 distinct MMSI, format confirmed .zip, served from the DMA's S3 archive (web.ais.dk is dead, see docs/DECISIONS.md)
Open the Parquet with DuckDB; confirm column schema, row count, distinct vessel count. Done 2026-09-16 against the real 2024-06-05 day
Render one day of vessel positions on a static map. Done against the real 2024-06-05 day: outputs/quicklook_2024-06-05.png
Dockerfile and reproducible environment
Clean AIS: drop invalid MMSI, impossible coordinates, duplicate messages. process/clean.py, validated against real 2024-06-05 day: 17,239,519 -> 10,429,200 rows
Identity resolution: link MMSI to IMO, detect reused and orphaned MMSI. process/identity.py, validated against real day: 4,519 MMSI, 1,304 with valid IMO, 3,215 orphaned
Reconstruct tracks per vessel and segment into voyages. process/tracks.py, 6h gap threshold (parameterized), validated against real day: 4,751 voyages
Unit tests with synthetic cases for each cleaning pathology. Satisfied by the test suites built alongside P1-1/P1-2/P1-3: 54 tests total, all passing

Empirical coverage map: receive probability per sea grid cell and vessel class. detect/coverage.py, built over 2024-06-01..2024-06-30: 9,265 cells, 42,968 (cell, ship_type) estimates with >=20 pairs. FLAGGED: selection-bias/circularity in the short/long-gap-ratio method (62.5% of estimates are exactly 1.0, none below 0.5) -- see P2-1b and docs/DECISIONS.md

Fixed P2-1's coverage-map bias via cross-vessel corroboration: detect/liveness.py, a tri-state verdict (receiver_alive/area_dark/no_evidence) with leave-one-out on both the concurrent count and the historical baseline. coverage_probability/grid.parquet retired outright (62.5% of estimates were exactly 1.0, no discriminative range). Validated on the full real 30-day window (11,556 gaps): 85.0/2.5/12.5% split, duration-matched placebo clears the falsification bar for short-to-medium gaps (+19.0/+16.6 points) but only weakly for 12h+ gaps (+6.4 points) -- see docs/DECISIONS.md. Tramo B (coverage.py -> cadence.parquet) deferred to a future session

Detector 1: deliberate AIS gaps. detect/gaps.py: every consecutive voyage pair in voyages.parquet is a candidate gap, scored via detect.liveness.liveness_verdict on cells from both endpoints. Verdict -> probability table (receiver_alive=0.9, area_dark=0.15, no_evidence=0.5), clamped to [0.4, 0.6] for gaps >=12h per the known corroboration weakness there. All thresholds unvalidated defaults. 14 new tests (140 total), ruff clean

Detector 2: position spoofing. detect/spoofing.py, four independent checks over clean AIS, one row per detected event: impossible speed (>50kn implied via consecutive-pair great-circle distance, only for pairs >=60s apart), on land (point-in-polygon against ingest/landmask.py's Natural Earth land polygons, eroded 1.1km inward, cropped to a quantile-based bbox, land mask exploded via ST_Dump into small-bbox pieces, join chunked per day partition), synthetic circles (Kasa algebraic circle fit per voyage via bulk grouped SQL, not per-voyage queries; angular spread via mean resultant length), simultaneous positions (same mmsi/timestamp pairs >500m apart). New ingest/landmask.py downloads+lands the land polygons once. Fully closed: code unit-tested (180 tests, ruff clean), real 30-day run completed and corrected -- see docs/DECISIONS.md for all 5 real-data fixes, including a P2-4-session fix to ST_Distance_Sphere's reversed argument order in this DuckDB build (final counts: 10,098,760 events: impossible_speed 5,499, on_land 10,092,010, synthetic_circle 93, simultaneous_position 1,158). on_land's volume sanity-checked and explained by legitimate long-duration dockside dwell, not a bug.

Detector 3: ship-to-ship transfers, using the GFW definition. detect/anchorages.py (empirical coastal-anchorage mask, 15 tests) + detect/sts.py (the detector, 22 tests): episode segmentation fixing a 647-hour false-encounter artifact, GFW's structural hard gates, and a six-term rule-based confidence score (not a calibrated probability). Fully closed: 202 tests, ruff clean. Real 30-day run: 1,255,460 candidate episodes -> 1,689 survive the hard gates (mean confidence 0.382, 17.6 min), sanity-checked -- see docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/STATE.md.

Detector 4: identity anomalies. detect/identity_anomalies.py (8 kinds: no_valid_imo, name/callsign change+flapping, reused_mmsi, shared_imo with cross_mid, shared_identity) + detect/identity_anomalies.build_vessel_links (data/identity/vessel_links.parquet) + new process/mid.py. Reframed per P1-2: gates on 'ever validly Tanker/Cargo without a valid IMO', not the 71% global orphaned-MMSI rate. Real 30-day run: 265 events (no_valid_imo 91, name_change 47, name_flapping 60, callsign_change 12, callsign_flapping 22, reused_mmsi 1 matching process.identity exactly, shared_imo 18 with 14 cross_mid, shared_identity 14), 28 MMSI linked into 14 vessel groups, ~4.5min wall-clock. 32 new tests (242 total), ruff clean. A dedicated review pass found and fixed 4 temporal-leakage bugs before close -- see docs/DECISIONS.md.

Detector 5: declared-behaviour contradictions. detect/behaviour.py: destination_course_mismatch (declared destination matched to a port by name; flags median COG-to-bearing deviation >90 deg over >=10 points, >=20km from port, >=2.0kn SOG -- COG used instead of heading, 91% vs 76% coverage) + draught_change_unexplained (>=2m median-draught change between consecutive voyages with no port/anchorage or STS evidence in the gap). Both scoped to MMSI with a valid IMO (P2-5's reframing). Real 30-day run: 916 events (152 destination_course_mismatch / 117 MMSI, 764 draught_change_unexplained / 586 MMSI), ~55s. A dedicated review pass found and fixed three real bugs before close: an impossible knowable_at for the draught check (now window_end, whole-window not gap-bounded), an anchorage-evidence self-exoneration circularity (now leave-one-out, mirroring detect.sts's P2-1b fix), and ~24-30% of course-check events being stationary-vessel COG noise (now gated on SOG). 13 tests, ruff clean.

Measure agreement of detector 3 against the GFW Events API. ingest/gfw.py (fetch+normalise+bbox-filter) + detect/sts_agreement.py (matching+measurement), 26 new tests, ruff clean. Real run over the 30-day window: 116,966 raw global entries -> 58,359 unique GFW encounters worldwide, only 6 inside our Danish/Baltic bbox (52.15-60.09N, 2.42-17.88E) for the whole month -- confirms GFW's fishing-economy scope barely touches this region. Agreement: 0/1,689 detect.sts events matched (0/177 in the fishing-ship-type subset), 0/6 GFW encounters matched. Investigated the one case sharing a real vessel pair DMA also received (219007313/219004002, 2024-06-25): DMA's own AIS shows the pair at 374m apart then drifting past 2km within an hour, never sustaining <=500m for GFW's reported ~2h20min window -- the two providers' underlying position feeds disagree, not a code bug. Full detail in docs/DECISIONS.md.

Ingest OFAC, EU and UK sanctions lists, capturing designation dates. ingest/sanctions.py: fetch_ofac (streaming iterparse of sdn_advanced.xml, type-IDs resolved from the file's own ReferenceValueSets), fetch_eu (OpenSanctions mirror of the official FSF feed, webgate.ec.europa.eu 403s without a token), fetch_uk (UK-Sanctions-List.csv, grouped by Unique ID, earliest Date Designated). Landed combined at data/reference/sanctions.parquet. Real run 2026-09-21: 2,205 vessels (OFAC 1,540/1,528 with IMO, EU 2/2 with IMO, UK 663/662 with IMO), designation dates 1989-01-05 to 2026-08-24, all day precision. 34 new tests, 315 total, ruff clean

Join sanctions to vessels by IMO (MMSI surfaces in the output, sanctions lists carry no MMSI of their own) and quantify match rate and ambiguity. process/sanctions_match.py: reuses process.identity.VALID_IMO_SQL against sanctions.parquet's own imo column, one output row per (sanctioned-vessel-record, matching mmsi) pair at data/identity/sanctions_matches.parquet. Real run 2026-09-21, NOT near-zero as initially expected by analogy with P2-7's GFW comparison: 205/2,191 checksum-valid sanctioned records matched (9.4%), 164 distinct mmsi -- UK 130/662 (19.6%), OFAC 75/1,527 (4.9%), EU 0/2. 41 of 164 matched imo corroborated by both OFAC and UK; 0 mmsi_is_reused matches, 0 double-distinct-imo-same-mmsi cases (both implemented and unit-tested, just not exercised by this window); 1 of 2,192 real sanctions imo values failed the checksum. A real CAST-error bug found and fixed before this result was trusted: wrapping VALID_IMO_SQL in NOT(...) breaks DuckDB's filter short-circuit, fixed with an anti-join instead -- see docs/DECISIONS.md. 15 new tests, 330 total, ruff clean

Build the labelled vessel-month panel. features/panel.py: 346 tests pass, real run over 2024-06 landed data/processed/vessel_month_panel.parquet (21,146 rows, 4,881 with a valid imo, 147 sanctioned only after window_end). analyst-review's original 4 defects all fixed: imo IS NOT NULL population restriction documented as a hard blocker, all 5 sanctions-derived columns renamed to a label_ prefix with a guard test, the false 'sts reproduces exactly' claim corrected in docs/DECISIONS.md, and the P4-3 blocker list rewritten complete and accurate in features/panel.py's own docstring (gaps safe, sts worse than stated, synthetic_circle confirmed backdated, static whole-window identity features flagged as the largest prerequisite).

Discriminative check with exposure-normalized features: a go/no-go gate. Done 2026-09-22. features/panel.py gained n_observed_hours/n_observed_days (from detect.liveness, survives discarding clean data) and 21 rate_* columns (RATE_BASE_COLUMNS x per-voyage/per-observed-day/per-1000-messages, nullif-guarded). New model/discriminative_check.py: 147 positives (sanctioned after window_end) vs 4,717 negatives (never sanctioned) within imo IS NOT NULL, AUC + 95% bootstrap CI + Mann-Whitney p per feature, unmatched and (ship_type, n_observed_days quintile)-matched scopes. VERDICT: GO, narrowly -- only n_draught_change_unexplained (raw + all 3 rate variants) discriminates as expected in both scopes (AUC 0.60-0.65); gaps/spoofing remain discriminates_opposite, sts/identity_anomalies/destination_course_mismatch remain no_discrimination in every scope, unrescued by normalization or matching. P3-4 may proceed per the plan's literal rule, but Phase 4 must report this as one detector family working, not five -- see docs/STATE.md and docs/DECISIONS.md's 2026-09-22 entries. Two real bugs found and fixed before trusting the result (a DuckDB same-name-alias resolution bug in the rate SQL; an ignored n_bootstrap argument in the check module). 360 tests (13 new), ruff clean.

EXECUTE AFTER P4-0, not before. Per-window storage pipeline so windows sampled across 2022-2024 can be processed with a disk peak of ~1 window instead of the sum of all (30 clean days = 14.2 GB today). Four parts: (1) [DONE 2026-09-22] partition liveness by day into data/coverage/liveness/date=.../part-0.parquet and make liveness_verdict accept a directory, INCLUDING the critical denominator fix -- with disjoint windows the naive span over-counts baseline_hours_available and silently biases every verdict toward no_evidence. Migrated over the real 2024-06-01..2024-06-30 window (3,988,982 rows, matching the legacy file exactly) and verified byte-for-byte against detect.gaps (74,546 candidates, identical verdict breakdown, zero row-level diffs). A real performance bug (naive per-call directory stat loop) found and fixed via a cached directory listing -- see docs/DECISIONS.md. (2) [DONE 2026-09-22] every detector (anchorages, spoofing, sts, identity_anomalies, behaviour) plus process/tracks.py and process/identity.py now write data/<kind>/window=<start>_<end>/part-0.parquet atomically instead of one whole-range file; new process/ship_type.py fixes the hard blocker (features/panel.py's _build_ship_type and detect/identity_anomalies.py's _build_ship_types both read clean partitions directly before this). detect.gaps deliberately NOT converted (the plan's own consumer, not producer, list). Consumer defaults (mmsi_imo_path/voyages_path/liveness_path/spoofing_path/sts_path/identity_anomalies_path/behaviour_path/anchorages_path) point at window=* globs, except ship_type_reference_path, which resolves to the caller's exact window to avoid widening an already-documented whole-window-no-month-bound limitation. Real-window equivalence check (delegated to a background agent) passed for all 9 real builds against the existing legacy artifacts -- exact row-count match on 8/9, the 9th (spoofing, 10,098,758 vs 10,098,760) traced to a pre-existing non-deterministic tie-break in unmodified SQL, not a regression; a handful of float-last-bit/mode()-tie-break diffs elsewhere, same non-regression class. 381 tests, ruff clean. Full detail in docs/DECISIONS.md's 2026-09-22 P3-4/A2 entry. (3) [DONE 2026-09-22] process/thin.py: day-partitioned downsampled tracks (data/tracks/thin/date=.../part-0.parquet, one row per (mmsi, 5min bucket)) for the Phase 5 map and manual review, never for re-detection. Day-partitioned like A1's detect.liveness, not window-partitioned like A2's detectors. Real run over the full 2024-06-01..2024-06-30 window: 452 MB, 26,333,818 rows, 21,146 distinct mmsi across 30 day-partitions (matches features.panel's own roster exactly); one real day measured first (18 MB/day) confirmed the default 5-minute interval stays within the plan's 10-25 MB/day budget. A real navigational_status-vs-nav_status column-name mismatch found and fixed before the first real run. 9 new tests, 390 total, ruff clean. (4) [NOT STARTED] pipeline/window.py CREATES artifacts and never deletes, pipeline/prune.py deletes opt-in with quarantine-first (.trash), per-day fingerprints, a .no-prune kill switch, a max-days cap and gates re-evaluated at deletion time. The re-download drill (delete one day, re-fetch, verify the fingerprint matches) is the gate that must pass before any deletion is trusted. Full spec: Part A of the approved plan at docs/PLAN_P4-0_P3-4.md
